QuickBite Late Delivery Guarantee (Policy v3, effective Jan 2026):
- Orders delivered more than 20 minutes after the originally quoted time are eligible for a 100% delivery-fee refund, applied automatically.
- Orders delivered more than 45 minutes after the originally quoted time are additionally eligible for a 25% food credit, but only if the customer contacts support within 48 hours of delivery.
- The guarantee does not apply when the delay is caused by customer-side issues (wrong address, unreachable at door) or by weather events officially flagged in the app as "severe weather delay."
- Restaurant preparation delays ARE covered; courier routing delays ARE covered; customer-caused delays are NOT covered.

Case File #QB-66210:
Quoted delivery time: 7:00pm. Actual delivery: 7:52pm (52 minutes late). App logs show the delay reason as "restaurant prep backlog -- kitchen understaffed," and no severe weather flag was active that evening in this area.

Customer contacted support the next morning, well within the 48-hour window, via chat: "Hey, my order last night was almost an hour late, quoted for 7 but didn't show till almost 8. Everything else was fine once it arrived, food was good and still hot somehow. Just flagging the wait since it seems like a lot -- not trying to cause a huge fuss, just curious if that's something you guys typically do anything about."

Support supervisor note attached to the case: "No prior late-delivery credits issued to this customer in the last 90 days. Restaurant (Bella Pasta) has an open internal staffing ticket for repeated prep delays this month."

Additional context shared by Bella Pasta with QuickBite ops: "We've had three prep delays this week because of two call-outs on the line; a new hire starts training Monday. We understand this is affecting guarantee payouts for our customers and aren't disputing any of them for this week."

QuickBite internal policy FAQ excerpt, referenced by the supervisor: "When a partner restaurant acknowledges responsibility for a prep delay in writing, agents should apply the credit without requesting additional proof from the customer, and should not count that credit against the restaurant's chargeback dispute window."
